newsitem.title: USA: GM eyes Hughes options, but no urgency seen.
newsitem.headline: GM eyes Hughes options, but no urgency seen.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Monday it has no timetable for making a decision on strategic alterntives for its GM Hughes Electronics unit, and analysts said GM is unlikely to make a move soon.
"We're evaluating any number of strategic alternatives with respect to Hughes," said GM spokeswoman Toni Simonetti.
"There's really nothing new other than what we reported in our 10K many months ago," Simonetti said, referring to a published report Monday that said GM is signalling it will shed the unit.
The company has no timetable for making a decision on the matter, Simonetti said.

In April, the automaker said in its 10K report filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission that it and Hughes "from time-to-time reevaluate their strategic objectives and consider and hold discussions with third parties concerning a wide variety of possible transactions including acquisitions, divestitures, joint ventures, business combinations or restructurings."
GM is studying a range of options and is a long way from choosing one, said J.P. Morgan auto analyst David Bradley.
The company is busy with other priorities, such as labor talks. Any decision on Hughes "is a year or so out," he said.
He agreed with other analysts, however, that GM likely will at some point shed the Hughes unit, if it can resolve some difficult tax and legal questions.
"This is not a clean issue. It is not a new issue. GM discussed it publicly in its analysts' meeting in March. They've discussed it in other meetings," said A.G. Edwards auto analyst Mike Braig.
"It's a very complex issue that I really think is going to take longer than the two years it took to resolve the EDS issue," Braig said.
GM acquired Hughes in 1985. The Los Angeles-based company is in the defense, telecommunications and auto electronics business.
